$comment: Anchor and extent metadata for every positioned coordinate keypath, used by the
layout editor to draw a correct bounding box and to move an element to the right
place. This CANNOT be derived from the coordinates file: `x` means a different
thing per element, and the truth lives in the renderer, not the schema.
It is a standalone file rather than annotations on _common.schema.json because the
$defs there are shared shapes (point, rect, named_point...) reused by elements with
different anchors, so there is no per-keypath place to hang this. Coverage is
enforced by tests/test_layout_anchors.py, which fails if a positioned keypath is
added to a coordinates example without a matching entry here.
anchor:  left        x is the left edge (text: the pen start; boxes: the left side)
center      x is the horizontal CENTRE; renderer calls center_text_position
right       x is the RIGHTMOST pixel; content grows leftwards
board-right pinned to layout.width - 1; x is not configurable at all
none        no x/y positioning (column offsets only)
extent:  text        single line of text; width = len(text) * font.width
scroll      scrolling_text clipped to a `width` window starting at x
box         filled or outlined rect of `width` x `height`
square      outlined square from (x,y) to (x+size, y+size)
diamond     base diamond inscribed in (x,y)..(x+size, y+size)
arrow_up    tip at (x,y), widens downward, half-width `size`
arrow_down  tip at (x,y), widens upward, half-width `size`
vline       vertical rule at x from y_start to y_end
squares     a column of `size` squares, one per entry in `squares` (y tops)
image       bitmap scaled into `width` x `height`
column      an x-only column position inside a list layout
NOTE: for every text/scroll element, `y` is the BASELINE, not the top edge. A
bounding box needs the font's ascent/descent, not just the font height.
$screens_comment: Which elements are actually drawn on each screen, as keypath prefixes. The
coordinates file holds every element for every screen at once, so an editor that
shows all of them is unreadable -- and worse, it invites moving something into
space that only looks free because the current screen does not use it.
'teams' and 'network' appear everywhere: the team banner is drawn last on every
game screen (renderers/main.py), and the network overlay sits on top of that.
inning.break.* is drawn only between half-innings, which is a sub-state of the
live screen rather than a screen of its own.
$derived_comment: Things the board draws that have no coordinates of their own. They are listed in
the editor so you can find them and see what governs them, but they cannot be
moved directly -- there is nothing to move.

atbat.pitcher_era.label: Pitcher ERA
atbat.pitcher_era.note: Drawn by __render_pitcher_text, not from its own coordinates. Its x is the leftmost column of atbat.batter_stats (which is itself measured back from the right edge of the board) and its y is the atbat.pitcher baseline, in the atbat.batter_stats font. To move it, move those two elements; to hide it, clear show_era.

atbat.batter.note: an 'AB:' label is drawn at x; the scroll window starts 3 chars in

atbat.pitcher.note: a 'P:' label is drawn at x; the scroll window starts 2 chars in

atbat.batter_stats.note: AVG/HR/RBI are laid out leftwards from layout.width-1; only y is configurable

batter_count.nohit.note: alternate position used only during a no-hitter

batter_count.perfect_game.note: alternate position used only during a perfect game

final.inning.note: center_text_position: x is the centre of 'FINAL' / 'FINAL 11'

inning.number.nohit.note: alternate position used only during a no-hitter

inning.number.perfect_game.note: alternate position used only during a perfect game

inning.arrow.up.note: size comes from the parent inning.arrow

inning.arrow.down.note: size comes from the parent inning.arrow

pregame.scrolling_text.warmup.note: used instead of the parent while the game is in warmup

teams.record.away.note: offset from the team name's end when teams.record.position is 'relative'

teams.record.home.note: offset from the team name's end when teams.record.position is 'relative'

teams.line_score.away.note: x is the RIGHTMOST pixel; runs/hits/errors are drawn right-to-left from it

teams.line_score.home.note: x is the RIGHTMOST pixel; runs/hits/errors are drawn right-to-left from it
